g.text: HURDLE & CARRY · LOCATE THE QUESTION'S TEST POINTS
Model optima and Q5's 8% hurdle and 15% carry
The model favors higher hurdles and lower carry. Q5's 8% and 15% are specified terms to evaluate,not unique optima discovered by the model.
An LP-value optimum within a chosen range is not the same as a reasonable negotiated term,which also needs market and contract evidence.
Carry cut from 20% to 15%, no hurdle assumed

At these inputs, the 8% hurdle without catch-up gives the largest gain of the three. With full catch-up, the 8% hurdlegives a smaller gain than the isolated carry cut — so the catch-up clause is essential to the evaluation.
Inception values. Common model baseline: 1.35% fee, 20% carry, no hurdle. Q5 terms are separate from the growth and discount assumptions.Scaled to a $750m modeled commitment from unrounded outputs.

Source: Q5 Analysis!C10:E10; Summary!C29:F29. Baseline OPERF NPV is $28.24m; the three alternatives give $30.96m, $48.88m and $45.90m — alternativescenarios, not additive steps. The maximum LP-only gain in the tested ranges is +$70.67m (zero carry, or a hurdle high enough to eliminate carry).
